title: Global Milk Ingredient Atlas
matching_rules: match_exact = the material itself as named on an ingredient list; match_related = derived ingredients (extract, oil, protein, ferment) kept distinct per the atlas rule. Regex, case-insensitive, applied to each listed ingredient name.
safety_note: Food composition is not finished-product concentration; brand claims are not efficacy evidence. Do not apply fresh milk, yogurt or homemade ferments to broken or irritated skin. Milk proteins can be allergens.

records.name: Cow's milk
records.composition: ~87% water; 3.0–3.9% protein; 3.3–5.4% fat; 4.4–5.6% lactose; minerals/ash ~0.7–0.8%
records.constituents: Caseins, whey proteins (including beta-lactoglobulin and alpha-lactalbumin), triglycerides, lactose, calcium, phosphorus
records.skin: Soaps, cleansers and creams; milk proteins/fats may contribute conditioning or emollience
records.hair: Milk-protein conditioning products; possible film formation and improved feel
records.evidence: Ingredient function is formulation-dependent; do not infer clinical benefit from food composition
records.safety: Milk-protein allergy; fresh milk spoils and is not a preserved cosmetic
records.regions: Global dairy markets; regional traditions vary
records.sources: FAO milk composition; comparative milk-composition reviews
records.traditional_use_notes: Dairy bathing and milk-based cleansing appear in historical and modern beauty narratives, but a specific practice should be tied to a named source/community before being treated as established.
records.regions_research_context: Global dairy markets; no single region owns the practice.
records.commercial_examples: No specific product example added in this pass; search by exact INCI and market.
records.verification_status: Tradition requires source-level verification; composition well established.
records.source_status: Mixed: core composition/ingredient identity varies by record; regional tradition and commercial availability require the per-record notes above.
